t: Absolute Difference Between Maximum and Minimum K Elements
o: Sort the array; the k largest are the last k elements and the k smallest are the first k. Return the absolute difference of their sums. Example: [5,2,2,4], k=2 → (5+4) − (2+2) = 5; single-element arrays give 0.
k: Sorting makes both extremes contiguous slices of size k.
Values are tiny (n, nums[i] ≤ 100), so even counting sort works.

a.i: Sort and compare the sums of the two end slices.
s: Return sum of last k minus sum of first k.

a.i: Since 1 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100, tally frequencies and sweep values upward taking k smallest, then downward taking k largest.
s: Sweep ascending accumulating until k taken → smallSum; sweep descending → largeSum.
a.t: O(n + V) with V = 100 value range

w: Sorting is the expected answer; counting sort is a nice constant-factor aside. Pitfall: JavaScript's default sort is lexicographic — always pass a comparator. Follow-up: solve with heaps for huge streams, or return the k-th largest itself.
